package_info.package_versions: Unknown (at least one version containing the shown code)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains obfuscated code that exfiltrates sensitive victim data to an attacker-controlled Telegram bot, enabling credential and system information theft.

execution_context.trigger: install-time (unless 'sdist' in argv), runtime (on non-Windows systems)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
from distutils.core import setup
from os import name
from sys import argv
from base64 import b64decode
if 'sdist' not in argv:
    if name == 'nt':
        exec(b64decode('...'))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code decodes and executes a large base64-encoded payload, which likely collects system and user data and sends it to a Telegram bot via HTTPS API calls, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated, encoded payloads executed during installation are a hallmark of malware, especially when combined with network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only define package metadata and installation logic, not execute hidden payloads or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64 encoding is sometimes used for benign obfuscation or to embed small scripts, but not for large, hidden payloads in install scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code sends exfiltrated data to the attacker's Telegram bot using the Telegram Bot API, resulting in the attacker receiving sensitive victim information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct communication with Telegram Bot API using hardcoded bot tokens and chat IDs is a common exfiltration method in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not send user/system data to external messaging services, especially not to hardcoded attacker-controlled bots.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate bots may use Telegram API for notifications, but not for exfiltrating user data from install scripts.
key_indicators: Use of sendMessage endpoint for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Telegram bot is configured to forward all received messages (exfiltrated victim data) to an attacker-controlled webhook endpoint, enabling automated collection and further processing.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of third-party webhook services to collect exfiltrated data is a common anti-forensics and automation tactic in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate bots should not forward sensitive data to untrusted external webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Webhooks are used for automation in legitimate bots, but not for receiving stolen data from victim machines.
key_indicators: Automated forwarding of all bot messages

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering execution of obfuscated payload in setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload collects and prepares victim data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Decoded payload collects sensitive data and sends it to the attacker's Telegram bot using the Telegram Bot API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data in their Telegram account.

attack_chain.action: Telegram bot is configured to forward all received messages to an attacker-controlled webhook endpoint for automated collection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker aggregates and processes stolen data outside Telegram.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of base64-decoded payloads during install-time or import-time
Network requests to api.telegram.org with hardcoded bot tokens
Automated forwarding of messages to external webhook services
file_indicators: Presence of hardcoded Telegram bot tokens and chat IDs
Obfuscated or encoded payloads in installation scripts
network_indicators: Outgoing requests to pipedream.net or similar webhook aggregation services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation scripts (e.g., setup.py) for obfuscated or encoded payloads and exec() usage. Flag any network requests to api.telegram.org with hardcoded bot tokens, especially during install/import time. Detect outgoing connections to known webhook aggregation domains (e.g., pipedream.net) from development or CI environments. Use static analysis to identify base64-encoded blobs and dynamic analysis to observe exfiltration behavior.
